chunks: Ahmad, from one of our companions, regarding the imprecation (Mubahala).

He said: 'Intertwine your fingers with his fingers, then you should say: O Allah! If so-and-so has denied a truth and acknowledged a falsehood, then strike him with a reckoning/thunderbolt from the sky or with a punishment from Your Presence, and you should curse him seventy times.'

key_terms.الْمُبَاهَلَةِ: Imprecation; a ritual of invoking divine curse upon the liar in a dispute.
key_terms.بِحُسْبَانٍ: With a reckoning or thunderbolt; a specific type of divine punishment from the sky.
key_terms.تُلَاعِنُهُ: You curse him; the act of invoking mutual curses.
key_terms.جَحَدَ حَقّاً: Denied a truth; the condition for the curse to take effect.

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual procedure and supplication for Mubahala in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific ritual mechanics of Mubahala, emphasizing the physical interlocking of fingers as a sign of solemnity before invoking divine retribution against the party denying the truth. It highlights the Shia scholarly understanding of the supplication as a direct appeal for Allah to strike the liar with a 'hukman' (account/punishment) from the heavens, reinforcing the spiritual weight of the oath. The mandate to curse the opponent seventy times underscores the completeness and intensity of the imprecation in this context.

en.hubeali: Ahmad, from one of our companions,

‘Regarding the imprecation, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Intertwine your fingers into his fingers, then you should be saying, O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! If it was so that so and so has denied a truth and acknowledge with a falsehood, so either Hit him by a thunderbolt from the sky or with a Punishment from Your<sup>azwj</sup> Presence’, and you should curse him seventy times’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad has narrated from certain individuals of our people about al-Mubahalah this:

“Crisscross the fingers of your hand with his fingers and say, ‘O Lord, if so and so has rejected a truth or has professed a falsehood, make him suffer misfortune from the sky or a painful punishment by Your command and then (the parties) renounce each other seventy times.’”
